prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1290; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change. Insured reports the other vehicle moved into their lane without signaling. Both drivers stopped at scene. Police report requested. Claimant reports back strain and is now represented by counsel; all further contact to go through their attorney's office.

Entry 2: Spoke with insured to confirm the sequence of events. Insured states the adjacent vehicle was in the blind spot and did not check before merging. Photos of both vehicles received, showing damage to the driver-side rear quarter panel of insured vehicle and passenger-side front fender of the other vehicle. Liability appears to lean toward the other driver, pending review of the police report.

Entry 3: Received letter of representation from claimant's attorney. Claimant alleges lower back strain and has been referred to a physical therapist. Medical records requested through authorization signed by claimant. Attorney requests that no recorded statement be taken from claimant without counsel present. Noted in file.

Entry 4: Reviewed the police report. Responding officer documented the other driver as having changed lanes into the insured's path. Witness statement from a passenger in the insured vehicle is consistent with insured's account. Vehicle damage estimate is in progress. Medical bills and treatment notes from claimant's provider are still outstanding.

Entry 5: Followed up with claimant's attorney regarding the outstanding medical records and the status of the physical therapy treatment. Attorney indicates the claimant is still attending sessions and expects to provide a summary of treatment shortly. Claim remains open with liability under review. Next step is to finalize the repair estimate and await the treatment summary before evaluating the injury component.
